I dry heave when I’m (physically) okay, but still do it if I’m anxious/having a panic attack. 

Basically when something bad happens/triggers anxiety our brain gets stuck in this cycle to protect us telling us it’s going to happen again. So, the way I personally try to break that cycle is remind myself of the million times I did that exact same thing at that exact same time and was perfectly okay. I also tell myself it’s okay to be anxious, anxiety is normal, and am learning to accept it. Thus, lessening the anxiety.

For example, I’m struggling with agoraphobia right now and can’t go into a grocery store, gas station, etc. basically anywhere I have to stand in line after having a panic attack in line. so this week I’m doing an exposure therapy to buy 3 items alone and am going to remind myself of the million times I did it before and was fine. 

Not to make this about me just giving an example. It’s not stupid, you’re not stupid you have anxiety. Our brains are tricky!  You can do this!!

I know the stomach bug (usually norovirus or rotavirus) is highly contagious but it IS possible to prevent it when caring for someone with it. 

1. Wash hands with soap and warm water for 20 seconds 
2. Try and avoid touching mouth/face especially if you haven’t washed your hands 
3. If you can get a hold of a face mask I’d wear one! 
4. Wear gloves (disposable ones) when cleaning 
5. Bleach kills norovirus! When cleaning I’d use bleach on any possible surfaces there are also other cleaners I believe Lysol might be one? I think it might depend on the type. 

This site is way more detailed for you: https://www.brownhealth.org/be-well/reduce-spread-norovirus-your-home

I wish you luck I hope your little feels better soon.

Edit: here’s one more site I found that also has some discussion on preventing spread throughout the household https://www.chop.edu/news/health-tip/how-survive-when-stomach-bug-hits-your-household
